title: Trump Honors Immigrant Tech CEOs Hours After Vance Suspends Microsoft Green-Card Filings
excerpt: Five of the six tech leaders who received America's top science and technology medals on Thursday are immigrants — honored the same day the administration accused Microsoft of abusing the visa system.
body:
• President Trump presented the National Medal of Science to Elon Musk, Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang and Lisa Su, and the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Satya Nadella and Michael Dell, at Thursday's "Science: A New Golden Age" summit in Washington — his first time awarding either honor.
  • Five of the six honorees are immigrants — Musk (South Africa), Brin (Russia), Huang and Su (Taiwan), Nadella (India). Dell was born in Texas.
  • Hours before the ceremony, Vice President JD Vance suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini from the PERM green-card sponsorship program, accusing Microsoft of laying off 6,000 U.S. workers while obtaining 6,300 H-1Bs and nearly 3,000 green cards.
  • What it means for you: the PERM suspension freezes new employer-sponsored green-card steps at the eight companies — existing H-1B status is not revoked. With roughly three-quarters of H-1B approvals going to Indian workers, anyone with a pending green-card filing should speak to immigration counsel; a proposed $103,265 H-1B fee and a $70,000-per-student OPT fee are not yet final.

WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump awarded America's highest honors for science and technology to six tech billionaires on Thursday, five of them immigrants, hours after his vice president accused one of their companies of abusing the visa system.

The ceremony capped the White House's "Science: A New Golden Age" summit at the U.S. Institute of Peace. SpaceX founder Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su received the National Medal of Science. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Trump called the group "national treasures," comparing them to his uncle, MIT professor John Trump, who received the Medal of Science in 1983.

For more than three decades, Satya Nadella has been a key figure in the transformation of Microsoft, revolutionizing the company and empowering businesses, students and consumers from all over the world.

— Donald Trump, presenting the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Nadella

A crackdown announced hours earlier

Before the medals, the day's harder news came from Vice President JD Vance, who announced that Microsoft was being suspended from the federal PERM program, which requires employers to demonstrate no qualified American workers are available before sponsoring foreign workers for green cards.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XEFa6Hnas_4

"You cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants," Vance said. He accused Microsoft of firing 6,000 U.S. workers last year while obtaining 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. The administration suspended seven more companies alongside it: Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini. Vance also said nine universities, including Stanford, MIT and Harvard, face investigation over alleged fraud in the J-1 exchange visa program.

Microsoft pushed back the same afternoon, saying about 80% of its roughly 6,000 H-1B filings last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of existing employees, and that its remaining new filings equaled about 1% of its U.S. workforce. Microsoft ranks fifth among U.S. H-1B employers; Amazon is first.

Asked about the apparent contradiction of honoring Nadella while sanctioning his company, Vance said the administration would "continue to support Microsoft and have a great relationship with Microsoft."

The diaspora stake

The juxtaposition landed hardest on the Indian community. Nadella, who arrived in the U.S. as a graduate student in the late 1980s, is the most prominent Indian-born executive in American corporate life — and he accepted his medal the same day the administration put the Indian IT consultancies that sponsor thousands of Indian workers under the microscope. Nearly three-quarters of H-1B approvals go to workers from India, making every swing at the program a diaspora story first.

For workers at the eight suspended companies, the impact is immediate: the Labor Department will not accept or process new or pending PERM applications from them, which stalls employer-sponsored green-card cases. H-1B visas already held are not canceled by the suspension, but anyone with a pending PERM case should consult immigration counsel without delay.

I was an immigrant, and my parents brought us here to pursue the American dream. It's an incredible honor, and something that could only happen here in America.

— Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO, speaking to NBC News after receiving the National Medal of Science

What's next

On immigration, the pressure is building on multiple fronts: a proposed $103,265 H-1B fee is still working through rulemaking and is expected to face the same legal challenges that killed an earlier $100,000 attempt, and the Department of Homeland Security has separately proposed a $70,000 fee per international student participating in the Optional Practical Training program. Carnegie Mellon president Farnam Jahanian, speaking at the summit, warned that recruiting the world's best talent requires an immigration system that can bring them here and keep them here.
